subject.title: [Bug]:  Isolated cron session agent loop continues consuming tokens after run marked "ok"

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to cleanup after each run, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle flag?
rationale: Both directions have open pull requests and user impact: the default-cleanup path addresses the reported token leak, while the one-shot-only path preserves a stricter existing interpretation of `deleteAfterRun`.

options.title: Default isolated recurring jobs to cleanup
options.body: Land a reconciled version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95950, including explicit upgrade behavior for already-persisted omitted values.

options.title: Keep deleteAfterRun one-shot-only
options.body: Close or reject the default-cleanup direction and continue through the strict validation path in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 with clear operator guidance.

options.title: Require explicit operator choice
options.body: Avoid changing defaults and instead add warnings, doctor guidance, or CLI migration prompts for isolated recurring jobs without an explicit session-retention choice.

recommendation.title: Default isolated recurring jobs to cleanup
recommendation.body: Land a reconciled version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95950, including explicit upgrade behavior for already-persisted omitted values.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged cleanup path that the remaining default decision would activate for recurring isolated cron jobs.
